tips.comment: Entered my notebook over this trip at Catterick on the 12th of May when making good headway against the rail but no room to challenge and squeezed. Not suited by the drop in trip over a mile and a quarter at Redcar 2 weeks later and this trip will suit more.
No comment made

Bosphorus Rose is today’s standout bet at Ripon (3:15). Trained by Sir Mark Prescott, this progressive runner comes off a win and remains well-handicapped. With consistent form (333-1) and ideal race conditions, she’s primed for another strong performance.
In good form over last few runs and should run well again over this trip . trainer has agood record at this track

Milteye has spent much of his near past as a hurdler but has recently joined the Bethell yard and has been reinvented as a flat, mid-distance animal. Still with some scope to improve further Milteye may well be the value here

EVELYN'S PHOENIX is a well treated four year old with potential to peak fourth-up for this spell. He was a winner last summer at this track from a 2lb higher mark and has a win to his name on ground this quick. One of the bigger priced runners of interest.

TREFOR should take all the beating in the feature at Ripon this afternoon and 3/1 can be taken. The son of Invincible Army built on a 1.5l defeat on his penultimate start to win by 1/2l at Doncaster LTO when eased in class; he’s put back into C2 level today off a 4lb higher mark so must be competitive. He’s fairly lightly raced for a 4yo so we can’t be sure where his ceiling lies and a few positive favourite stats for IA boost claims further; a 58% SR (A/E 1.67) at northern courses, a 53% SR (A/E 1.59) on straight tracks and 50% SR (A/E 1.4) with sprinters.
Pals battalion has been very well backed, won at Newcastle in March and ran a respectable race when fifth last time out at Haydock at the start of the month

Michael Dods has suffered a nightmare season, however things are definitely looking up at last. He had a double at Thirsk on Tuesday, and that grand old veteran Commanche Falls could get back to winning ways here. The selection has lots of top handicap form on his CV, including here at Ripon, and was a promising second at Hamilton last time. If he's anywhere near the top of his game he can win for the first time since his Garrowby win of 2023.
Bottom weight second last time , six times course and distance winner , jockey in form , will be there at the business end of the race , great each way shout at 8/1 , Nap Each Way

Not the most consistent but was a good all the way winner at Thirsk two starts ago before no showing at York in a much deeper race last time. Conditions here much more in favor and looks good each way value in a shallow field.

Risky but the yard is firing on all cylinders and this horse is now rated 14lbs lower than last summer when he raced in group company.
Jockey rode a good race last time and will know this horses capabilities better today so he can place at least.
No comment made
Ran on inside the final furlong over a furlong shorter at Doncaster last month and should appreciate this extra furlong.

Grand old boy who landed a 14th career victory when striking at Wolverhampton in April. Not so good on turf these days but has been running well off this sort of mark this spring so can't see any reason why he shouldn't be bang there once again.

Backing Mark’s Choice, the seasoned 9-year-old gelding by Bungle Inthejungle, trained by Gemma Tutty, in tomorrow’s 6-furlong Racing Welfare Handicap at Ripon. He’s a genuine Ripon specialist with seven career wins on this track and a strong placing record from over 60 starts . Most recently, he ran a solid race at Thirsk on 6 June, finishing a respectable 4th of 12 over 6f on good ground??'staying on well inside the final furlong .
That Thirsk run showed he remains in good heart, and now running off a career-low rating of around 60 makes him a dangerous contender after dropping in class . At Ripon, where his record is particularly strong, expect a patient ride to bring him into the race late. With his track aptitude and recent fitness, he offers genuine each-way value at around 9/1.

Roundhay Park is a shorter price than he should be considering his form figures this year. However he has gone well here previously which is vital to his chances. He ran quite well in a Veteran's handicap at Catterick two races back. He failed to build on that at Redcar last time, but there were excuses, badly drawn, failed to get cover, and the high numbers completely dominated the race. Alex Jary claims five, and with his rating way lower than it was at his peak, his chance looks promising.

This R Varian trained 3-y-o filly has finished a close second in her first two races over one mile two furlongs the latest at Goodwood on good ground 26 days ago when running on well inside the final furlong to only be beaten a neck behind the James Horton trained Liberate so with Ray Dawson booked to ride she can make it third time lucky today

Fidelius drops into Class 4 company after competing respectably in higher grades, showing strong early-season form. Trained by sprint specialist R M H Cowell, he’s well drawn and looks well handicapped for this 5f test. With solid form and ideal conditions
No comment made
Hard to believe his form has been this bad since last win at Southwell back in March of this year but now operating 1lb lower than last winning mark so has a chance tomorrow.

This lightly raced S bin Surroor trained 4-y-o filly has only run four times winning on her latest start over one mile at Kempton eight days ago when showing a fine turn of foot inside the final furlong to beat the C Gordon trained Ombrecell by two lengths so with Dylan Hogan onboard she can defy her five pound penalty and follow up today

I’m backing Hitched, the 5-year-old Cotai Glory gelding trained by David Simcock, in tomorrow’s Mac Cosmetics Magic Mile Handicap. He enters this off the back of a strong season, winning at Lingfield on April 18 and again at Newcastle and Lingfield in late 2024 and January??'showing excellent consistency and adaptability on all-weather surfaces . Although his recent fifth over 1m 2f at Windsor on June 2 wasn’t eye-catching, his strike rate of 8 wins and 6 places from 31 starts underlines his competitive edge .
Now dropping back to a mile on Chelmsford’s polytrack??'a surface he has thrived on??'and racing with a lighter lens after stepping up in trip, he is fitter and well-treated off his current mark in a class 4 handicap. Expect him to break smartly, settle mid-division, and produce a sharp turn of foot coming into the final furlong.

Won first 2 runs last year but struggled LTO when only 14 of 15 here over C&D at the start of thi smonth but not reading too much into that considering that was first run back in 14 months so expecting a much more competitive effort this time out.
No comment made
Ran green over this trip at Newmarket on racecourse debut in a Class 2 last month. Should improve for the experience and drops in grade to Class 4.
No comment made

Indalo for Roger Varian appears very 'well in' at Chelmsford tonight and warrants the utmost scrutiny in a race where he appears to hold all the aces. Has won on all weather and creditably on turf the slight increase in trip proving no problem last time at Hamilton. Back on all weather at Chelmsford I expect him to return to winning ways

Worth a look back on the all weather considering the form he showed on this surface in France
Rated 14lbs including the jockeys 7lb claim lower than when doing well in a c3 around a year ago so should be able to get competitive with conditions and weight terms in his favour.
Has struggled for form this year but now opearting 2lbs lighter than last winning mark and helped by a drop down in class and experience of this course might just be enough to cause an upset.

Charles Darwin could be another two year old winner like Gstaad for AP O'Brien and Ryan Moore although he did not last the distance in his first race at the Curragh over 5f he has made all comfortably at Navan over 6f and Naas over 5f and looks to have improved with each race.

With breeding and stable form with this type of horse, NAVAL LIGHT looks a justified play at the price, he looks the most likely one to conquer the hot favourite and we can play each-way at this price too.

AFJAN could be anything which could be said of many of these juveniles. A compact Mehmas-sired sprinter who created a favourable impression when winning on debut in France and related to multiple speedsters he could be the each-way value against the odds-on market leader.
First Legion won on debut last month and followed up with a good second in listed company and clearly improving so more is expected in today's G2
Won his debut in a class 2 at York over 6f on good to firm (good in places) before dropping to 5f 10yds for a Listed event at Sandown finishing a decent 2nd of 7. Jockey S Foley retains the ride.
Did seem to stay last time but his winning debut was very promising. from a leading yard and looks good enought to take this despite the bad draw. big player
Finished a good 2nd of 13 at leicester on debut last month. 3rd and 5th that day have won since and with improvement likely for having had that run holds an each way chance

with a hot favourite here there is good each way value to be had with the stables second string at a big looking 33/1 especially with an extra place up for grabs.he ran green despite winning at salisbury and with further improvement he should get involved here

In the first-time tongue strap, LONDON BOY is sure to progress after being well on top when beating Mission Classified in a Maiden Stakes at Brighton 10 days ago. Jockey David Egan has won once in one ride (100%) when aboard & London Boy has also won once in one run (100%) over 5 furlongs. One to watch.

Charles Darwin could blow this lot away and can’t be taken lightly, but it looks fairly open otherwise and I’ll chance Clear Force being overpriced out of a race that has worked out well already. That does in theory mean he’s held by First Legion, and he had no obvious excuses for getting beaten by that horse at Sandown. That said, he wasn’t beaten all that far, and drawn alongside the favourite I’d hope he can be dragged into this a long way. With further distance in his pedigree perhaps a bigger field scenario can work in his favour, and if it does then he’s entitled to be a shorter price than he currently is. 2nd on speed figures, he goes for last years winning trainer.

Exclamation has podium finished in all three outings so far in this fledgling career with finishes of 3rd, 3rd and 2nd and they were reasonable quality fields so worthy of merit and while stepping up in opposition here looks incredibly priced even for the place part only but I wouldnt full discount he win equity being greater than 1% either.

This race has given big price winners before with a 150/1 winner in 2023 and 50/1 winner in 2022. Worth taking on the likely odds on favourite because of that. This horse won LTO at Nottingham and the 2nd went on to achieve an RPR of 89 on his next run. If he does the same he will be competitive in this.

Irish Fighter small each-way, is a risky tip. I'm placing this tip only because of the good odds, he'll need lots of improvement but never say never, perhaps a place finish is his best hope. Finished 2nd on debut on the AW over 5f , into a much better race today but a good, different jockey to that debut run is booked today and this jockey often has horses outrun their odds, the jockey - SDS, has already done well on horses at big odds at Royal Ascot this week. Risky small each-way tip.

Illinois is a genuine Group 1 performer over 1m4f and if he gets this trip he looks like a banker for Aiden O'Brien, who is a master at producing these extreme distance stayers. He came a close second to the high class Jan Brueghel in the St Leger last year over 1m6f and he is a relaxed horse, so he has every chance of getting this extreme trip of 2m4f.
Ran a fine 2nd in this race last year and warmed up nicely with a smooth victory at Sandown in a group 3 contest. Nothing to prove here and should be the clear form pick.

Candelari is fairly unexposed with only five runs winnning four of them including his latest in a Group 1 at Longchamp over fifteen and a half furlongs. A Frankel gelding he has both speed and stamina and two and a half miles could be within his stamina limitations.
Bizarre this ithought in a interview this week Gosden stated Sweet Willam was the one in this yet its drifting all day long ?...ill stake my claim to it ew

Trawlerman should do all he can to test the stamina of Illinois here which makes it interesting tactically. The French horse looks a stout stayer but has it to prove on the ground. I’m wary of Sweet William having his day, but it was Dubai Future that I thought was overpriced. You have to forgive him a dire effort last time when miles behind the French horse, but notably he just hasn’t gone with any zest with soft in the going description so I’ll take that as an excuse there. He was so far back, and that doesn’t reflect his prior form in Meydan when he actually beat Trawlerman in a slowly run Dubai Gold Cup. He acts well on quick ground, and if this does turn tactical and he can stay in touch, the old boy could once again show a turn of foot to match his younger rivals. Just 2-3lbs to find on official ratings, he could be swinging early out the back, but if he can stay in touch round the final bend I hope he can come home strongly.

WONDER LEGEND is not fully exposed on turf and a curious statistic shows that all-weather form especially Kempton year-on-year translates well for this royal meeting. He has potential to stay this most extreme of distances with not much to find on official ratings , so the feeling is he is overpriced with potential to surprise.

Coltrane has been close on both outings so far this calendar year with a 2nd placed finish at Ascot in April backed up by another runner up finish at Sandown last month, look to go one closer here and for that level of consistencey to be rewarded.

First time running for Michael Bell and was a staying on winner of the Sagaro Stakes. The Sagaro is one of the key form races for this one. His second run for Michael Bell here but also his second run after a break during which he changed stables and had another wind op. The tongue tie also stays on. Its a tasty looking race and I'm just not sure Yashin should be such a huge price.

Detain has not run on going this fast before and all three of his wins have been on the allweather but he has run well in both French Classics this Season and should be in the first two home here hopefully in front.
Rock solid form with a 4th in a group 1 and a head 2nd at Epsom but left his challenge too late. Steps down in grade and should take all the beating.

If the front two under perform then High Stock could be the beneficaery Won Wood Ditton in good style on debut after did well in the circumstances having missed the start and raced far to keelny at Chester on next start going down a neck to Aiden O'Brien hot pot

TORNADO ALERT sees ace Australian jockey James McDonald teaming up with Saeed bin Suroor having previously combined with six placed efforts. Jockey McDonald has ridden plenty of Godolphin-owned runners back home and fourth in the Derby failing to stay he is eased in class and should go close back down in distance.

Was a massive eyecatcher on debut and a few of my shrewdy mates jumped on this one to note as highly rated and potentially smart. We were gobsmacked when beaten next time at Sandown but wac all dressed up with nowhere to go before powering home in the manner of a decent horse who'll enjoy a step up in trip. Gets that here and rates a first class bet as will relish this stiff finish. Big horse with loads of scope and yard have had most run well here already over the first two days. Massive engine and massive chance to my eye in what doesn't look the deepest race and this one brings the most potential.

Despite needing to take another step forward, improving sort ARABIAN FORCE is in excellent hands who still looked green when beating another useful sort Gladius in a Novice Stakes at Salisbury 5 weeks ago. He has won once in one run (100%) over 1 mile 2 furlongs & has won twice in two runs (100%) on good-to-firm or similar going. One to watch.
GLITTERING LEGEND was a listed winner last time out and could be dangerous if improving on that. You can't deny the credentials on the bear form and there are each-way claims for sure.

Finished 2nd at Naas on debut in September and followed that with a win at navan in April. Demoted to 3rd after passing the post in front last time. Further improvement still likely and holds an each way chance

Fancy this quite a bit overpriced I think holds its form well and appears to be improving a tad Joseph's horses often get overlooked here but he is a magnificent trainer in his own right not beaten all that far in a group 3 in Ireland despite not having a great run through ground should suit chances

Sea Scout has 2 wins inside the last 4 outings and while did not impress last time out at Epsom was impeded early and appearaed unsettled from that monent onwards so will to allow a pass on that one and at these odds for the levels of performances shown previously can't go far wrong to keep inside ehre.

It is a tough task, but TIBERIUS THUNDER is not one to write off yet after being hampered/denied a clear run when 5th to Thrice in the Group 3 Gallinule Stakes at the Curragh 4 weeks ago. He has won once in four runs (25%) for trainer Adrian Murray. Lively outsider.
GOsden and O'Brien throwing the kitchen sink at this one but CATALINA DALCARPIO could usurp them all. Less exposed them some but not too green either and the step up to this trip could be perfect.

The Andrew Balding runner looks the one to be on here, following her excellent second in the Musidora at York to the subsequent Oaks runner-up Whirl. This step-up in trip is certain to bring more improvement & she looks the bet of the day.

The O'Brien / Moore combination have won last 2 renewals of this race in 2024 with Port Fairy & 2023 with Warm Heart so looking for 3 timer . Her 2 wins have both came at Naas 7f in August 2024 & her last run 40 days ago over 10.5f in Listed Oaks Trial on good by 1L . Is upped in trip & untried at 12f but shouldn't be a problem .
Looks like a step up in trip is needed after 2rd place finish at Newmarket. Has won and finished 2nd at Kempton in previous two starts.

Not an obvious staying contender and towards the bottom of these on ratings. But she did beat Caspi Star on the AW with relative ease in the end. That horse reopposes here having chased home the Oaks winner since to put some gloss on the form. She’ll need to improve on her Chester handicap win since, but she did that with enough authority despite seemingly getting a bit lonely late on. The form tied her into the current Fav quite nicely to think she’s on the overpriced side despite having plenty to find on ratings. With no absolute standout I’m hoping it will be another one for Wathan.
Caspi Star is having a very impressive calendar year so far with a win and 2nd and a 3rd in just the three outtings to this point and shouldn't be too far away from the reckoning here.

This step up in trip might be an opportunity for Coolmore’s Japanese three year old to run a big race and I am backing Wayne Lordan will give Ecstatic every chance. Won last year in Tipperary and has been second and third at Leopardstown and the Curragh, this Ribblesdale Stakes looks competitive and I am backing Ecstatic outshines Garden Of Eden for Aidan O’Brien.

Ran out a comfortable winner on first 2 career starts at 1 mile and 1m2f both times at Lingfield. Finished third in the Group 3 Musidora stakes at York on penultimate start last month behind Whirl. Has since then finished 9th in the Group 1 Epsom Oaks probably not suited by the juice in the ground that day. Could go well on this quick ground and looks an each way contender for a yard in great form.

The Gosdens have a good record in this fillies race with three successes in the last six runnings and Understudy, who arrives in good form with a win at Southwell last time out looks capable of getting involved here at a rewarding price.

3 year old Wootton Bassett filly who has placed on her 2 stars this season. Has a bunch of decent runs in defeat in Group company and first time blinkers could do the trick here. Yard do well in this race although they are generally well represented in it.
Ran no sort of race when 6th of 8 in a Naas listed race and the writing was on the wall from half way when pushed along. Wasn't unfancied that day and can run into a place at 50/1,

Distance winner who won a class 3 last time out staying on strongly at the finish of 1m 3f 188yds at York on good to firm (good in places) under todays jockey and 82 rating. Rating goes up to 90 today stepping up to a class 2 after a refreshing 35 day break.
Last years winning jockey Ryan Moore opts for Serious Contender of the three Aidan O'Brien entries. Could be suited by the course if coming from off the pace.

One of my favourite races of the meeting and a race that often produces a Group performer. Sing Us A Song has shown gradual improvement upped in trip to 1m2f and his pedigree, being by Camelot and out of a Galileo mare, indicates there could be more improvement at this 1m4f trip. The trainer Ralph Beckett won this race last year with a similar sort.

Gunship only started racing in December, but has put up some remarkable perfomances. At Sandown I thought he still was quite green and he did well to stay in to third place. His last run on all-weather was good and the fast pace in that small field was definetly in his favour, which we can expect in this race. The runner-up has won twice since then, so Gunship looks well handicapped.

I'm backing the Appleby losers a treat this week but he's had some near misses and MASAI MOON is another who should give us a good run for our money. The each-way potential helps and hopefully this progressive sort from a decent stable can hit the top five.

Finished 3rd of 7 when made favourite last time out but was staying on in the closing stages of 1m 2f 40yds at Navan on good (good to firm in places) under todays jockey. Not A P O'Briens first string but extra yardage today will suit so nice ew bet @16/1 paying 5 places.

Lightening Mann finished 2nd in the London Gold Cup last time from a mark of 81 and although 4lbs higher here could still be well handicapped from a mark of 85. Prior to that he won on quick ground at Newmarket, with Merchant 1L back when giving the selection 5lbs. They meet on the same terms today after Merchant's win LTO, and the 4th that day has also won since which makes the form look strong enough. Quick ground suits him and he stays well. Has been bought by Australians presumably with a view to big prizes down under but can claim this en route.
Went off a strong 8/13f last time at The Curragh in May and Ran out a comfortable winner. Ryan Moore deserts him and his price has inflated but still totally unexposed. Good each way chance.

A 12f handicap. Four career runs for the selection, form 3-321. Irish raider.Improvement with each run. He was a smart maiden winner four weeks ago, pulling clear late on to win by 7L - A capable type in second that day. An opening handicap mark of 90 gives him a chance, this longer trip should suit him and he’s still unexposed.

Trainer Alan King has a good record at Ascot and fifty per cent of his runners at Royal Ascot have finished in the first six places over the past twenty five years. Daiquiri Bay represents him in this race and he appears to have a good draw in the big field and he has won a race this season.

Simon and Ed Crisford have yet to taste truimph here and they may be seeing a very big run appearing from Boatswain who is by New Bay and dam sire Lope de Vega, He has been stayoing on at teh finish in all three races with winning his first and then two seconds. Drawn in stall one, with jockey Mickael Barzalona who could be pushing his mount forward to be prominent and picking up when required to show twelve furlongs is what he has been crying out for and taking this race with reversing form with Masai Moon. With me typing this horse up, has moved from 40/1 to 33/1 tomorrow could be shorter.

Gets an 8lb swing with Merchant, and whilst more exposed than many of these he brings in some solid enough form as a result. It was a fair effort at York, and he’s hardly been disgraced since. It’s a fairly quick turnaround for the horse, but on the whole in an open race he looks a massive price. He has beaten 8/1 shot Sing Us A Song over shorter, and whilst more exposed than most he’s fairly unexposed at the trip, and the way he hung right handed at York would suggest he’ll prefer going this way round, and he certainly still looks well handicapped on his best form.

If you can forgive The Cursor his last run at Epsom he us a huge each way price in this race.
His run behind Bedouin Prince is strong form and he can outrun his odds here.

Ammes was not put up for winning a two horse race last time at Chepstow but the horse he beat Triple Gee went on to beat odds on Marnier next time out.Ammes wears first time cheekpieces and is one of the few that have already won at the distance.
Mafting followed two second placed efforts with a win at Redcar last time out and could put in a big performance here at a handy each way price.

Still a maiden after 5 runs 3 of those on all weather last season & 2 placed efforts at 8 & 10.5f . This season placed twice on turf at Cork over 10.5f on soft & at Roscommon over 10.5f on good & could keep place consistentcy at big odds now stepped up to 12f for 1st time .

Grecian Legacy is today's NAP, it's a risky tip because this is a good race with many good horses who are open to improvement so it's a small each-way tip only, extra places available each-way with a few different bookmakers. Has shown ability in all 4 runs on turf , hasn't finished out of the places with 1 win and 3 placed finishes. Excellent run in defeat at Epsom over 1m2f last time out, beaten only a neck where he stayed on well all the way to the line so that suggests this step up to 1m4f, is worth trying, but this is a better race than last time. Good to Soft ground last time, faster ground conditions today which may actually be more suitable and this slightly more straightforward course may be more suitable than Epsom was last time.

Raafedd looked very genuine at Newbury on his last start. He won that race so easily, while the opposition was far from bad. Both the runners which finished second and third went on to win races, one of them receiving a handicap mark of 92. That is also Raafedd his handicap mark, which seems too low with this evidence. Haggas does extremely well in these handicaps, but he'll need some luck in running with this many opponents.

This is ultra competitive and I'm torn between Teroomm and Fifth Column, but I just favour Teroomm who has won his last 3 races. He beat Afentiko who has got a pull in the weights from the last run but Teroomm has got a winning attitude and I think he will confirm the form. I will have a saver on Fifth Column especially with the Gosdens is great form yesterday.

Brave Mission has only run four times and he moves up in distance from seven furlongs to a mile having had two seconds and a win in his last three runs and looks good to go close in this 30 horse handicap.

Plenty of promise in 3 career starts including a wide margin win in a Maiden at Newcastle on penultimate start at the end of March. Good effort when 4th in a fast run 7f in a Listed race at Newmarket last month. Will prefer this return to handicap company upped in trip to1 mile for a yard that had a Group 1 winner here on Tuesday.
Arabian Story made all to win on UK debut last month and worth a chance with a trainer that tend to do well here plus I like having Oisin Murphy in the saddle for this EW 4P

Ralph Beckett will surely pop up with a winner at some point this week and it could be here with CONSOLIDATION who made a winning return in May and has had enough time off to be sufficiently freshened up for this.

PAROLE D'ORO is by a Royal Ascot winning sire and is a strong travelling type who seems likely therefore to be suited by this stiff track. Jockey Callum Shepherd should be able to hold on to him for as long as possible with this decent sized field and likely strong pace , so his chance on paper at least would appear strong with the tongue-tie now fitted.

Fearnot looks interesting have won over course and distance in a Class 4 handicap last month. He only made his debut in March when winning at Wolverhampton and was then placed at Kempton and Newmarket. He is 10lbs higher here but is sure to progress further and looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer

As ever, the Britannia is one of the most fiercely competitive handicaps of the meeting, with so many improving three year olds lining up. Going through the form is migraine inducing. The Gosdens are having a good week, and the willing Fifth Column looks one that can provide a nice each way return.

Have been keeping a close eye on this one who was a massive eyecatcher behind Terroom on seasonal debut making late gains. Is better off at the weights and has top apprentice booked so connections must mean business here. Was conceding the reopposing Terroom a fitness advantage at Haydock so should reverse places here and ag the odd looks huge value. Handled fast ground on debut when bumping into the smart Symbol of Honour and looks on a fair mark in this.

Aiden O'Brien and Ryan Moore on a big price runner, which can be strange, normally favourite. Serengeti has been in used as a pacemaker plus racing on rain softened ground did not help his cause at Naas. Today he is racing on his own merit and has good to firm ground to stride out well over, which can see this colt by Wootton Bassett being a serious player here.

In the each-way market, Shout looks an interesting contender at 20/1. A dual winner last season over sprint trips, he has been gradually stepped up in distance this term and has hit the frame on both outings, including last time out over this course. That day, he completely missed the break by several lengths, something he simply can’t afford to do in a field as competitive as this. However, the Simon & Ed Crisford team have given him a decent break since then and now reach for the hood for the first time, suggesting they've trained him specifically to iron out that issue. If the headgear has the desired effect, I can see him running very well, especially as the extra furlong is likely to suit. A live each-way player at big odds.

THE FINGAL RAVEN looks a consistent sort who has a good winter and been close in some decent quality races in the middle east. Could be more than ready to go handicapping in the UK and has real claims if he takes to it.
this is ultra competetive but arctic grey looks a decnet punt at 25/1.he won on his handicap debut and a 5 pound rise might not be enough to stop this likely improver

Bumped into a subsequent Listed winner last time in the shape of Amiloc who is now rated 109 which shines this mark of 95 in a fairly good light. He’d previously split some solid yardsticks at Kempton to add some substance to the thought that this mark is workable. I don’t mind a low draw for him as he could well nab the rail on the far side and run his own race. An overall lack of pace could play into the hands of those that are sitting up with it, with the risk he is just a bit too gassy and sets it up for something to come just off him. He’s a fair price though, and looks worth a swing to me.

In form Andrew Balding yard running a 3 year old Kingman colt in a class 2 mile handicap. Seasonal debut last time out and placed in this grade and trip at Sandown. Should come on for the run like a lot of Andrew Balding's do. Notable jockey booking.
The Johnny Murtagh trained Iceford clicked last time out when winning well at the Curragh over seven furlongs and could go well here trying a mile for the first time.

Supido hasn't been with this trainer for too long so could have a bit more to offer for this yard. Ran well in defeat over a shorter distance last time, kept on very well late on so this step up in trip may see him do better. These ground conditions will be the quickest he's raced on , not proven on Fast ground but he has some fast ground form in his pedigree which offers some hope of a decent run from Supido.

I cant resist having a small stake on this one. Basically, the price is too high (the selection is 160.0 on betfair at time of writing. The horse has done little wrong and the trip looks ok. Johnston and Fanning are a good team as well. Small each way stake

Speculative each way bet here on a well bred gelding out of Too Darn Hot and with Invincible Spirit as the dam's sire, he is related to some previous winners. Looks likely to improve with experience and could benefit from the drop in trip after racing over the extended mile and a quarter at Chester last month.
Impressed winning in debut run at Doncaster last June and after a series of difficult runs, I do think he will be better suited to handicaps and given his ability, looks a bit overpriced to me.

Brise Noir has so far shown his best form over further than today's 1 mile distance so it may not be ideal but, he showed good early speed last time and fast ground should suit. Still very early days for this horse in its career, open to some improvement but that is needed , this race will be tougher than last time but this horse is lightly raced overall so some further progress can't be ruled out. Very small each-way tip, i like the odds. It's a race where I'm trying to find horses who may run well at big odds.

Mississippi River a Lopez De Vegas colt stays this mile and looks to have chances in the Boylesports Rated Race today. This is a non handicap and Mississippi River is well treated by conditions of the race. He won a maiden and finished second twice in two handicaps this season. He has further improvement and looks a horse to back today

English Oak has managed to get himself to a mark of 100, only 1 higher than when he won this with ease on same conditions last year. His last run was encourageble, and Wathnan racing have showed that they are very capable of reviving horses for this festival as they did with Haatem on Tuesday.

A small neck shy of winning when finishing 3rd at Ascot latest early May in field of seventeen runners. Was close twice at Curragh previous to that in larger fields at the mile distance, so the step back to seven furlongs made a difference.

Never So Brave changed yards to Andrew Balding in Oct and returned in a C2 last month after being gelded and only missed out by a nose when second and I would expect more now second up with Oisin Murphy who is on a 28% strike rate for the last 14 days with most of those win being when running for AB

All five previous runnings of this rcae have been won by a four year old. Roi De france is one of a number of four year olds in todays race. The Gosden horse has to conced weight all round and have chosen to give Ryan Moore the ride. He has been dropped a pound from his last run and is weraing cheekpieces for the first time. Favourites have not had a good record in this race so a chance is taken that Roi De France can produce his best on the day and win.
A nose 2nd in the Lincoln in March and it's hard to forgive him that loss as it cost me plenty of money but returning after wind surgery and may have been held back with this race in mind.

RAMAZAN is a no doubt well handicapped runner often aimed high and there has been an upturn in the form of the Richard Fahey trained runners in recent days. That bodes well for this experienced mature racer who is fourth-up this term and with a talented claiming apprentice aboard he makes each-way appeal.
A 4 times winner between 7f and 1 mile who won very cosily in a fast run race iver 7f at Doncaster last time out 12 days ago and looks a big player despite a 6lbs penalty.

4 year olds have good record in the race winning last 5 renewals . Horse is relatively unexposed only 6 career runs so far with 2 wins at Yarmouth over 8f on good to firm & class 2 at Newmarket over 7f on good . Has ran twice this season both at Newmarket in class 2 races , was placed in 1st of those & was last of 6 last run 48 days ago but place claims back on cards again today .

The last time Witch Hunter ran off todays mark of 103 was when winning this race in 2023. Has run some decent races off higher marks since and I'm hoping back here in a big field off a competitive mark he returns to form.

Another typically impossible race to read, with several holding claims on paper. I'm siding with a long shot in Divine Libra, currently available at 20/1. He looks to be building towards peak fitness after two runs this term, including a slightly unlucky effort last time out at Chester, where he found little room in a tight finish for the places. There's plenty of solid form in his book ??' notably a two-length defeat to Myal at reappearance, which ties him in quite closely with Never So Brave, who despite carrying a 4lb penalty sits towards the head of the market. Divine Libra was well fancied and finished sixth in this race last year when denied a clear passage, so it’s fair to assume this has been a long-term target. The booking of James McDonald looks a significant plus, and he's worth an each-way play at the price, with bookies going 6 places.

The 5yo ran well for good trainer Andrew Balding as a 3yo and was rated 111 at one point - now racing off a 100 mark. Seven runs last year for a new trainer in the middle east, a couple of respectable runs. Now with a new trainer after being gelded. Back from a 5 month break with a nice run at Chester in a quality handicap and was a close 3rd of 13, made the more impressive as he was drawn wide and raced very wide throughout - and runners that race on that path do tend to be well beaten well before turning into the straight. He has top jockey William Buick booked for the ride.

The stiff 7f on quick ground is perfect for No Retreat's running style. He didn't quite stay a mile last time and Meydan's turning 7f was too sharp. He's been campaigned over longer and shorter but this setup quick ground straight track plays right to his abilities.

MYAL cannot be overlooked, who is still on the upwards trajectory after producing another career-best effort when beating fellow rival Never So Brave at Chester 3 weeks ago. Jockey Rossa Ryan has won once in one ride (100%) when aboard & Myal has won six times in eight runs (75%) over 7 furlongs. One to watch.
APIARIST has got a real finish in the locker so if a gap opens up and he hits it, from a likely pretty decent position on the track, he could get involved when it matters most.

Finished 5th of 18 over this course and distance in October and arrives having won on both of last 2 starts. Drop back in trip likely to suit for hat trick attempt and likely to be there or thereabouts

Northern Express is a course and distance winner and was 5th to English Oak in this race last year off 103 and he has now drifted back to only 101 and is three pounds better off with English Oak than last year.

Array returned in April from a whopping 546 days break to a decent C3 third and last month he was at the back of the pack when fifth of five but that was still less than 3L from the winner and has been a G2 winner in the past so I would expwect more today with Colin Keane to help out EW 6P
Impressed winning at Chester last month and does have ability so not surprising mark remains unchanged this time out but hoping he can show similar form to 2024.

YORKSHIRE has continued in fine fettle this term and his form ties in closely with MYAL who is my nap for the race. However, it would be no surprise to me if Bethell and Rodriguez are able to reverse Haydock placings on these revised terms.

Cerulean bay is the one I am picking for the big upset in the last of the day. The two Davids (Probert and O'Meara) are cobining and hopefully to slay Goliath for the second time in history - this time at Royal Ascot. Needed first two runs and that fifth at Chester was an improved showing. I feel the formline is a bit better than it looks on paper and I suspect they've probably had a few issues to iron out but he has the draw to capitlise this time, as history suggests for this race. Four of five wins to date have come when he's been drawn within the first six barriers and he gets barrier four here. This is not a great race for favourites but horses who are fourth up perform well in it and that's the way CB comes into this open field.

Jayyash's latest outing in Qatar was a clear career best effort. He is a winner over today's distance on a firm surface. Jayyash is consistent, having finished in the first three places on ten occasions from 13 outings. The booking of the in-form Mickael Barzalona takes the eye.
Fancy this to run well at Royal Ascot meeting no real form just a hunch as I like the trainer and jockey combo hopefully gets in the money

City Of Poets learnt from his first run where he failed to make all and finished in 2nd place. He was much more relaxed last time when making all at Lingfield winning by over four lengths. It will be a fast going 7f race for him at Wetherby but he should relax round the bend into the straight.

Fan club for me will be the one to beat here at a very nice price being dropped back down to 7f is going to be the key to this horse getting a win under his belt, fallon/haggas get on great and have an incredible strike rate together im playing this on the nose as im confident this horse will win.
Angela's Baar almost got up to win at Pontefract finishing well over 6f, the extra furlong at Wetherby should suit and she should win.

Winner of this race last year and althoug on a higher mark here has gone well off higher still in the past.
Jockey takes off a crucial 3lbs and comes here in great form and has an excellent record riding for this trainer.
Looks a good bet to follow up last year's win even though recent form is somewhat less than encouraging.

Although her recent form reads modest??'well down the field in her last three starts, including Kempton, Lingfield and Southwell on all-weather earlier this spring??'her juvenile win at Kempton under Hollie Doyle suggested she had plenty in reserve . But the breathing issue may have held her back until now. First-time-out after wind surgery, some sprinters can run below their best, but many show real improvement in the very next outing or two after recovering .
Wetherby’s sharp 5½-furlong straight will suit a filly who can settle quickly and use that extra breathing freedom to come home strong. If Lemos De Souza’s team have timed her return carefully, she could run into the frame??'or better??'at decent each-way odds, especially if the early pace is strong.

Led towards the finish but headed final stride over a furlong further in Class 4 company at York 5 days ago. Remains on the same mark, should be suited by the drop in trip and ease in grade to Class 5.

Veteran who hasn't won for a while but has slipped down the weights and best effort so far this season when 4th off this mark at York on Saturday. Something similar should see him bang there this evening.

YAAJOOZ started the season pretty well with competitive looking runs at Pontefract and Thirsk and if you are prepared to forgive the last time out run at York, which I am, then you can consider him here. That came in a higher grade, and a tough race for the grade too, so he looks to have claims at a workable weight back in this company.

Only 1-21 and yet to win a handicap but started his season in good form with placed efforts at Thirsk and Nottingham before a poor performance at Doncaster last time. Needs to bounce back but should run well if doing so.
Just one win from 21 runs makes for grim reading and barren run continues as it's now been 14 runs since last win back in 2023 but might have a chance now with dropped mark and 3lb claimer.

Candle Of Time should get he revenge on Rose Of New York who beat her two lengths into 4th at Carlisle over a mile. That was her first run since December and she did not get a clear run and is now much better off at the weights.

This S & E Crisford trained colt has finished second in his first two races over six furlongs and five furlongs on good to firm ground the latest at Wetherby 17 days ago but found the well backed D O'Meara trained Rogue Supremacy 2 1/4 lengths too good so with L Morris taking over in the saddle it looks like a win today

Royal Accord won over 6 furlongs here at Lingfield in April and won again at Brighton two weeks later. Placed at Newmarket and Brighton since he should appreciate this first attempt at 7 furlongs and looks the most likely winner

Linear spirits handicap debut here being upped in trip to where she has ran best over 7f it's a weak race and this horse will probably drift to a lot bigger odds but don't let that put you off. This horse looks the type to keep progressing
We were unfotunate with VITALLINE last time out when he got bumped early, but he finished strong and should be winning soon as definitely running into form.

Moutai steps up in trip tonight and this could be a move that can see him having the stamina to see this ten furlongs out well, with being on a flat course than like at Hamilton with last run that has a hill.

This former course and distance winner was sent off second favourite in a Class 3 at Windsor earlier this month but trailed in 7th of 9 over 6 furlongs. He raced in a Class 2 at Ascot over this trip in the race before that beaten 3.25 lengths off a mark of 83. He races off 82 here and with Oliver Searle in the saddle has another 5 pound to be taken into consideration to put him on an attractive effective mark with the step up in trip looking likely to suit.

Carthusian should be up to winning this maiden. He was second to Scandinavia, (who finished 5th not beaten far in a Group 2 at Ascot today), on his first run and with improvement can take this for his trainer Jessica Harrington who is in good form.

Won a maiden iover 1 mile at Yarmouth in a fast time last September for previous trainer. Finished well into 4th place over 7f at the Curragh on seasonal return last month when making debut for this trainer. Will prefer thisstep up to 1 mile and a top apprentice rides knocking off a handy 3lbs and looks a leading contender.

Friary Road looks far to big a price in this maiden for older horses. He won bumpers at Listowel and Punchestown last October and although beaten in his next two starts they were at Listed and Graded level. He was second in a Dundalk maiden in February on Flat debut but that was only over 1m4f. The step up to 1m7f should suit and he can go well at big odds
Cost 37,000 euros as a yearling and sire was a top class middle distance horse. Can make a winning fist of this.

FERRYBANK caught the eye in a big way latest in behind those placed. He gets a relatively quick turnaround likely having found a suitable handicap opportunity for his shrewd trainer and sharper/ready now he makes maximum appeal.

A 3 times winner twice over this 7f trip who finished well into 4th over this CD last week beaaten around 2.5 lengths behind todays forecast Favourite Finsceal Annie. Has a 6lbs pull at the weights with that rival today so could well turn around the places.

It would be folly, in my opinion, to completely write off Michael Grassick’s 6-year-old mare AMANIRENAS here, especially sitting at the bottom of the weights. She steps back up to her preferred trip of 7f and returns to Leopardstown, where she’s run well in the past. She’s now a whopping 15lbs lower than her last winning mark - an eye-catching drop.
Now, you might be thinking, “Well, she’s obviously a stone lighter because she’s been running backwards,” and that’s a fair assumption. But it’s important to note this daughter of WAR COMMAND just hasn’t been running over her ideal distance. Five of her six best runs have come at 7f, and two of those came right here at Leopardstown.
Yes, she’s fallen in the handicap like a stone, but she didn’t disgrace herself last time out at Fairyhouse over 6f just 13 days ago. That effort on unsuitably short ground suggested there’s still life in her yet. The return to 7f, quicker ground, and the booking of Gavin Ryan - who holds a 25% place strike rate here over the past five years - all give cause for renewed optimism.
Overlook her completely and you might regret it.

Rated 17lbs lower than last summer so looks like he must have some kind of chance given his record in handicaps around this level.
Interesting jockey booking taking his first ride on this horse.

Stayed on well from the back of the field to finsih 5th of 18 over this CD 13 days ago from a wide draw given too much to do. The form has been biisted by the winner going in again and Tilani runs here off the same marl and could go close if able to lay up closer to the pace tonight.

Methgal looks interesting at a big price in this 8 furlongs Leopardstown handicap. Trained in Britain by Karl Burke as a two year old he was far from disgraced in two decent maidens at Haydock and Goodwood before finishing 3rd at Ayr. Although unplaced in both starts since moving to Ireland he only faded late on last week at Cork and with cheek pieces added for the first time he is worth a small EW bet with 5 places on offer

The price looks fair at 33/1 for Cian Hughes’ 4-year-old gelding THOMPSON GUNNER, who has yet to make an impact in six turf starts. That said, his most recent run at the Curragh 27 days ago offered a glimmer of hope. Despite finishing 13th, for a brief moment half a furlong out, it looked like he might outrun his massive 50/1 odds and at least threaten the places. He eventually faded, finishing 7½ lengths behind, but it was far from a disgrace.
Now, this son of HIGHLAND REEL drops in grade, loses 3lbs, and gains the assistance of 5lb claimer Wayne Hassett - who boasts a strong 34.09% place strike rate here in Dublin over the past five years. That stat adds a layer of intrigue, especially as the gelding now runs 8lbs lighter overall.
While he may still be finding his feet, this looks a more winnable contest. It could be too early to expect fireworks, but there was enough in that last effort to suggest he might run better than the market expects once again.
A hope? A chance? Perhaps just enough of both to sneak into the frame this time.

HAUGHTY runs for a shrewd dual-purpose operation and this five year old mare could be interesting back racing on the level given her early career flat form in Britain. She will not come undone with this turf handicap mark , so she merits a market check.

Harbanakar was winning for the 4th time when taking a course and distance handicap in April. He has gone up 6lbs for that but is still 8 below his previous winning mark and looks at least a good EW bet with 5 places on offer

AMAVASYA is a three year old filly in open-age handicap company who merits close inspection. Her recent form at this venue was encouraging indeed and she should be open to considerable progress. Now with the yard among the recent winners she rates the value play.

Twice a winne over 1 mile for previous trainer who finished 5th over 1m1f here last week on soft ground behind todays predicted favourite Smaoineamh Sile. Will prefer this better ground and is 7lbs better off tonight so looks an eaxh way player with 5 places.

Noble Andy is still a maiden after 9 starts but looks interesting off his current mark. His best finish was at Bellowstown last October but he ran well to be 5th at Fairyhouse over 10 furlongs last month when fading near the finish. He is 3lbs lower today with blinkers that were worn at Bellowstown back on. Over 9 furlongs he looks a good EW bet with 5 places on offer

FLEETFOOTSOLDIER is not highly-tried on turf and is well treated against his overall profile. The yard will come alive soon this flat season and can be worth keeping on side when doing so. With an encouraging effort latest he can go close now.

TOMAHAWK KING should be capable as a five year old exploiting his current lowly handicap mark. He does not necessarily boast any strong form when fresh , but assuming the yard have him ready then he should be highly competitive. The market can provide further clues.

EAGLES WHISTLE might be worth chancing , she hasn’t troubled the judge yet but has hinted ability and her day might not be far away .. didn’t show a whole pile on the all weather but 2 recent turf runs were encouraging , she responded well for pressure LTO in listowel ,flew home, suggesting the extra furling will suit.. prior to that in Killarney met interference and flew home when the gap came… this mile 1 looks sure to suit .. I think a chance can be taken ..
